Q: How do you see the entire command history in interactive Python? A:

(Untested on MacOS: if possible, could someone please check?)

From within the python3 REPL for version 3.13+ in "fancy" mode (default, syntax colouring, blocks of code, etc) ...

Enter "history mode" by pressing F2 , which presents the history of the current REPL as if it were piped into less - once in history mode there'll be a prompt similar to this one (press q to exit history mode):

 /home/brynk/.python_history line 7032/7076 (END) (press h for help or q to quit)

Now type the key-sequence -O (hyphen then shift + o)

Log file:

Then type in a filename or path and press enter

Log file: ~/py3-hist.aug26

DISCUSSION

If i have multiple python [-B, -i] interpreters running in the same environment, i find that the contents of ~/.python_history are probably out of sync.

In the new REPL mode (ref) you can enter "history mode" T.Hunter'25 which is a view of the REPL history similar to (based on?) the less utility, for this specific REPL instance.

Once in history mode you can also press the h key to bring up the associated help, which will change the prompt in the help section to this:

HELP -- Press RETURN for more, or q when done

From within help press q to go back history mode

Here's the relevant part in help:

...

  -o [file] ..  --log-file=[file]
                  Copy to log file (standard input only).
  -O [file] ..  --LOG-FILE=[file]
                  Copy to log file (unconditionally overwrite).
  -p pattern .  --pattern=[pattern]
                  Start at pattern (from command line).
...

Q: Open and close websites in batch A:

I've tried this code, hope it's good for you:

What i've done is do a while loop, for you to choose how many times will the loop run.

I set the timeout as 10 seconds but you can change it for 5 seconds.

@echo off
set /A x=0
:while
if %x% LEQ 2 (
    echo %x%
    start /max chrome.exe https://www.google.es
    timeout 10
    taskkill /F /IM chrome.exe > null
        set /A x=%x%+1
    goto :while
)
